title: Proverbs 8 — Wisdom calls, and was beside YHWH at the founding of the world

verdicts.reasoning: hălōʾ-ḥokmâ tiqrāʾ ûtĕbûnâ tittēn qôlāh: lower-case 'wisdom' with the feminine pronoun (ASV practice). Exact.
bĕrōʾš-mĕrômîm ʿălê-dārek bêt nĕtîbôt niṣṣābâ. Exact.
lĕyad-šĕʿārîm lĕpî-qāret mĕbôʾ pĕtāḥîm tārōnnâ: qeret 'town'; the speech (vv 4-36) runs without outer quotation marks. Exact.

ʾălêkem ʾîšîm ʾeqrāʾ wĕqôlî ʾel-bĕnê ʾādām: 'O men' for the rare plural ʾîšîm; anarthrous bĕnê ʾādām 'the sons of human' under central ben-adam. Philologically literal; the English is stiff, which is founder point B, not a translation error.
hābînû pĕtāʾyim ʿormâ ûkĕsîlîm hābînû lēb. Exact.
šimʿû kî-nĕgîdîm ʾădabbēr ûmiptaḥ śĕpātay mêšārîm. Exact.
kî-ʾĕmet yehgeh ḥikkî wĕtôʿăbat śĕpātay rešaʿ: 'abomination' (central toevah). Exact.
bĕṣedeq kol-ʾimrê-pî ʾên bāhem niptāl wĕʿiqqēš. Exact.
kullām nĕkōḥîm lammēbîn wîšārîm lĕmōṣĕʾê dāʿat. Exact.
qĕḥû-mûsārî wĕʾal-kāsep wĕdaʿat mēḥārûṣ nibḥār. Exact.
kî-ṭôbâ ḥokmâ mippĕnînîm ...: third-person reference inside the speech noted (cf. 3:15). Exact.
ʾănî-ḥokmâ šākantî ʿormâ wĕdaʿat mĕzimmôt ʾemṣāʾ. Exact.
yirʾat YHWH śĕnōʾt rāʿ ...: the possible gloss is translated (in all witnesses). Exact.
lî-ʿēṣâ wĕtûšiyyâ ʾănî bînâ lî gĕbûrâ. Exact.
bî mĕlākîm yimlōkû wĕrôzĕnîm yĕḥōqĕqû ṣedeq. Exact.
Source checked: Leningrad reads kol-šōpṭê ṣedeq; the many-MSS/LXX/ASV ʾāreṣ is recorded. Keeping L is the declared MT baseline. Exact.
Source checked: Ketiv אהביה, Qere אֹהֲבַי; Qere translated (ASV the same). Exact.
ʿōšer-wĕkābôd ʾittî hôn ʿātēq ûṣĕdāqâ. Exact.
ṭôb piryî mēḥārûṣ ûmippāz ûtĕbûʾātî mikkesep nibḥār. Exact.
bĕʾōraḥ-ṣĕdāqâ ʾăhallēk bĕtôk nĕtîbôt mišpāṭ. Exact.
lĕhanḥîl ʾōhăbay yēš: yēš as noun 'substance' (ASV); petucha kept in Hebrew. Exact.

Re-parsed: YHWH qānānî rēʾšît darkô qedem mipʿālāyw mēʾāz. 'created' rests on the create sense of qnh (HALOT; Gen 14:19, 22; Deut 32:6; Ugaritic qny; KAI 26), the LXX ektisen, Targum, Peshitta, NRSV and NJPS, and the birth verbs of vv 24-25. The note gives the other side fairly and by name: ASV 'possessed', Aquila/Symmachus/Theodotion ektēsato, Vulgate possedit, Vawter's 'acquire'. It also says the line differs from the canon's English 'possessed'. The coincidence with the canon's French 'm'a créée' therefore has an independent lexical and versional basis. rēʾšît darkô is adverbial, with the appositional construal recorded.
mēʿôlām nissaktî mērōʾš miqqadmê-ʾāreṣ: nsk II 'install' (ASV 'set up', cf. Ps 2:6), skk 'woven' derivation recorded and not adopted. Exact.
bĕʾên-tĕhōmôt ḥôlāltî ...: Polal ḥyl 'brought forth' (birth language); 'depths'. Exact. Non-blocking: Ps 33:7 has 'the deeps' for the same plural; either is ASV.
bĕṭerem hārîm hoṭbāʿû lipnê gĕbāʿôt ḥôlāltî: Hophal ṭbʿ 'were sunk', the same rendering as stable job-woh 38:6 ('its bases sunk', checked); ASV 'settled' recorded. Exact.
ʿad-lōʾ ʿāśâ ʾereṣ wĕḥûṣôt wĕrōʾš ʿaprôt tēbēl: 'earth' || 'world'. Exact.
bahăkînô šāmayim šām ʾānî bĕḥûqô ḥûg ʿal-pĕnê tĕhôm: 'skies' (created sky), 'inscribed a circle', 'the deep' as Gen 1:2. Exact.
bĕʾammĕṣô šĕḥāqîm mimmāʿal baʿăzôz ʿînôt tĕhôm: 'clouds' (KJV 'clouds'; BDB/HALOT), so that šāmayim (v 27) and šĕḥāqîm get two English words. Lexically grounded; the canon does not quote this verse.
bĕśûmô layyām ḥuqqô ... bĕḥûqô môsĕdê ʾāreṣ: ḥōq 'boundary' as job-woh 38:10; 'his command' (pîw) with the literal sense in commentary. Exact.

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (FR 'comme architecte'; EN 'as one brought up with him')
verdicts.reasoning: Line approved. Re-parsed wāʾehyeh ʾeṣlô ʾāmôn wāʾehyeh šaʿăšuʿîm yôm yôm mĕśaḥeqet lĕpānāyw bĕkol-ʿēt: 'a master workman' (ASV, NRSV; LXX harmozousa; Akk. ummânu; Wis 7:21 technitis) is a defensible inferred choice, and the nursling (Aquila; Fox) and adverbial readings are given. Revise (commentary only): the reception note says the canon's quotation 'has ... the craftsman reading, which is also the reading of the line'. That is true of the French ('comme architecte') only. The canon's English edition has the KJV 'as one brought up with him', the nursling reading (TBWTT-3:278 EN). Replace the note's last sentence with: "The canon's French has 'comme architecte', the craftsman reading; its English edition has 'as one brought up with him', the nursling reading. The canon itself is divided, and the line follows the ASV, not either wording." Make the same correction in the overlay entry amon-master-workman-proverbs-8-30.
mĕśaḥeqet bĕtēbēl ʾarṣô wĕšaʿăšuʿay ʾet-bĕnê ʾādām: 'the inhabited world of his earth'; anarthrous 'the sons of human' (founder point B). Petucha kept. Exact.
wĕʿattâ bānîm šimʿû-lî wĕʾašrê dĕrākay yišmōrû. Exact.
šimʿû mûsār waḥăkāmû wĕʾal-tiprāʿû: prʿ 'neglect'. Exact.
ʾašrê ʾādām šōmēaʿ lî ...: anarthrous ʾādām 'the human' (generic; English needs the article), ASV 'the man'. Exact.
Source checked: mōṣĕʾî mṣʾy [māṣāʾ] ḥayyîm; Qere māṣāʾ translated ('has found life', ASV 'findeth'), Ketiv recorded. Exact.

wĕḥōṭĕʾî ḥōmēs napšô kol-mĕśanʾay ʾāhăbû māwet: ḥṭʾ 'miss' as the antithesis of mṣʾ in v 35; nepeš 'his own life' in the life/death antithesis (vv 35-36). Changed line verified; the rendering follows the Kings/Ezekiel overlays.

glossaryReview.reasoning: Site-by-site application of the founder's Kings-wave register ruling, checked verse by verse: physical sky 'skies' (Ps 8:2, 4, 9; 19:2, 7; 33:6; 147:8; Prov 8:27; Eccl 3:1; Job 37:3); dwelling or cosmic height 'heavens' (Ps 33:13 || mĕkôn-šibtô; 139:8 against She'ol). Ps 8:2 ('splendor upon the skies') is the closest call and is argued from v 4. Direct is appropriate.

'earth' at universal and cosmic sites (kol-hāʾāreṣ; ʾereṣ || tēbēl) is the reading of ASV, NRSV and NJPS, and the isaiah-woh precedent. 'land' is kept for territory (Prov 10:30; Job 37:13) and the stable 'wings of the land' (Job 37:3 = 38:13). Every site was checked. Agree with founder point C: promote the clause to central eretz in a later diff.

The lexical mapping is accurate and consistent with central ha-adam / ben-adam (direct) and with GEN-WOH-11:5 'the sons of the human' (checked). ʾĕnôš 'a mortal' and ʾîšîm 'O men' are sound. Flagged for founder point B. The articular/anarthrous split ('the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human', Prov 8:4, 31) is formally exact but yields stiff English, and in Biblical Hebrew the two forms are not distinct in sense. The corpus is now split three ways ('sons of men' ASV / canon-EN; 'children of men' 1 Kgs 8:39; 'sons of the human' Gen 11:5). Reviewer view: accept the editor's forms for coherence with the central entries, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 to them. If the founder prefers idiom, revert all bĕnê (hā)ʾādām sites together to 'the sons of men' with a string swap, and leave the singular ben-adam untouched.

citations: Wolff, Anthropology of the Old Testament (1974), ch. 2
glossaryReview.reasoning: The 'life' / 'soul' split was checked at all six sites. 'life' where a life is delivered from death or forfeited (Ps 33:19 || 'keep them alive'; Prov 8:36 in the life/death antithesis), as in the Kings and Ezekiel overlays. ASV 'soul' is kept for the self (Ps 19:8; 33:20; 139:14; Prov 10:3), with the appetite sense in commentary. Direct is defensible: BDB lists both senses.

citations: Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible (3rd ed., 2012)
glossaryReview.reasoning: All six pairs were verified in the Leningrad source (Job 37:12; Ps 139:6, 16; 147:19; Prov 8:17, 35), and all Qere are translated. The ASV-follows-Ketiv statements at Ps 139:16 and 147:19 are correct. No seventh pair exists: Prov 8:16 is a manuscript variant, as the editor says. Direct is correct.

Applied correctly at every listed site. MT Psalm numbering was verified (superscription = v 1 in Pss 8, 19; run into v 1 in Ps 139). The one vowel-only exception at Ps 8:2 is declared and justified: the MT impv. tĕnâ has no syntax after ʾăšer. Eccl 3:21 keeps the Masoretic articular participles and fully records the interrogative reading of LXX, Vulgate, ASV, NRSV and NJPS. Non-blocking: add 'KJV' to the Eccl 3:21 clause as the English witness to the MT pointing ('the spirit of man that goeth upward'), so that the entry does not suggest that every English version departs from the MT.

citations: Yeivin, Introduction to the Tiberian Masorah (1980), on the poetic accents
glossaryReview.reasoning: One line per Masoretic verse, divided at the main disjunctive; no outer quotation marks for Elihu or Wisdom (as stable job-woh 38-41); colon for Qohelet's internal speech (ASV). Verified across all nine chapters.

citations: Fox, Proverbs 1-9 (AB 18A), excursus on personified wisdom
glossaryReview.reasoning: Lower case with the feminine pronoun follows the ASV and leaves the personification / hypostasis question to commentary. The surveyed positions are correctly attributed.

citations: TBWTT ch. 3 (FR and EN of Prov 8:30)
glossaryReview.reasoning: Inferred is correct, and the three explanations are accurately surveyed: craftsman (LXX harmozousa, Akk. ummânu, Jer 52:15, Wis 7:21, ASV/NRSV); nursling ʾāmûn (Aquila; Fox); adverbial. One factual correction is needed. The rationale says the canon's quotation 'also has the craftsman reading'. Only the French does ('comme architecte'). The canon's English edition (TBWTT-3:278) has 'as one brought up with him', the KJV nursling reading. Replace the last two sentences with: "The canon's French quotation has 'comme architecte' (craftsman) and its English edition 'as one brought up with him' (nursling); the canon is divided, and the choice follows the ASV baseline." Make the same fix in the PRO-WOH-8:30 note.

Approve the entry and the class direct. šaḥaq 'fine dust' / pl. 'clouds' (BDB, HALOT), KJV 'clouds' at Job 38:37 and Prov 3:20; 8:28, and the stable JOB-WOH-38:37 all support it. Two corrections are needed before it is applied. (1) The wohChoice pre-lists Ps 89:7, 38 under 'clouds' but then says 'singular šaḥaq "fine dust" (Isa 40:15)'. At Ps 89:7 and 89:38 the form is the singular baššaḥaq and means the sky or the clouds, not dust. Reword the clause: "singular šaḥaq is 'fine dust' at Isa 40:15; the singular baššaḥaq of Ps 89:7, 38 ('in the sky / clouds') is decided at those sites." Either drop 89:7, 38 from the pre-listed sites or keep them under that clause. (2) The rationale names only the canon's French ('nuages solides') at Job 37:18. Add that the canon's English edition renders the verse 'the sky, which is strong', so that the record shows the canon is divided and the entry does not depend on it.

The content is approved. The appended rationale treats Prov 8:22 honestly as the most contested site (ASV, Aquila/Symmachus/Theodotion, Vulgate and Vawter for 'acquire'; LXX, Targum, Peshitta, NRSV and NJPS for 'created') and says that the direct class rests on the Gen 14 epithet, not on Prov 8:22. Ps 139:13 'created' is supported by NJPS and HALOT. The diff appends text to the base unchanged (verified). One mechanical fix: the appended wohChoice is joined without punctuation ('creator of heaven and earth Verbal clause ...'). Apply it as 'creator of heaven and earth. Verbal clause (Writings wave W1): ...'.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: All 36 lines checked. 8:22 'created' (LXX, Targum, Peshitta, NRSV, NJPS, HALOT) and 8:30 'master workman' (ASV, NRSV, LXX) have independent lexical and versional grounds, and the alternatives are given in the notes. 8:28 'clouds' is not a canon site. The 8:30 note overstates the canon's agreement and needs revision (canon EN has the nursling reading). That is a commentary-honesty fix, not leakage in the line. No flags.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 205 verses, the 17 overlay entries and the 16 central-diff ops were formed from the chapters, the Leningrad source files, the overlays, the diff, the 2.83.0 base and the canon-quotation file before wave-w1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's list of the three canon-coincident lines (section 1) confirmed the two commentary revisions: at Job 37:18 and Prov 8:30 the notes cite only the canon's French, whose wording matches the line, and omit the canon's English ('the sky'; 'as one brought up with him'), which does not. Prov 8:22 already shows the correct treatment. The report's six-pair Ketiv/Qere count was independently confirmed.

founderDecisionRecommendations.A-Ps-8:6-article-on-Elohim: Keep 'a little less than Elohim' without the article. The Hebrew mēʾĕlōhîm is anarthrous, the rule matches job-woh 1:9 and Kings clause 2, and the reception note already gives the canon's 'the Elohim'. Differing from the canon here is useful evidence that the line follows the Hebrew.
founderDecisionRecommendations.B-bene-(ha)adam: Accept 'the sons of the human' / 'the sons of human' for coherence with central ha-adam / ben-adam and GEN-WOH-11:5, and align 1 Kgs 8:39 ('the children of men') to it. The cost is stiff English at Prov 8:4, 31, and the Hebrew article on bĕnê (hā)ʾādām carries no difference in sense. If the founder prefers idiom, revert every plural site together to 'the sons of men' (string swap; drop the plural refIds from the ha-adam and ben-adam ops). Do not mix the two.
founderDecisionRecommendations.C-eretz-cosmic-earth: Agree. Promote the 'earth' scope clause (isaiah-woh + Writings) to central eretz in a dedicated later diff, after the parallel appliesTo merges have landed.
founderDecisionRecommendations.D-proper-names: Accept English forms in the four Writings books. Job 37 must match the stable job-woh chapters, and the four books must agree. Record the corpus practice as genre-split (narrative transliterated, poetry and prophets English) or settle it in one corpus-wide decision. Do not leave it implicit.
founderDecisionRecommendations.E-chesed-kindness: Confirm 'kindness' for solitary ḥesed now, before the Psalter grows (about 120 occurrences). It is the central wohChoice, consistent with genesis-woh and Kings, and lexically sound (Glueck; Sakenfeld). The loyalty sense stays in commentary, and the fixed pair ḥesed wĕʾĕmet stays under chesed-v-emet.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F-Job-37:18-clouds: No decision needed: 'clouds' rests on BDB/HALOT, KJV and stable job-woh 38:37, and 'strong' (not 'solid') keeps the line neutral. The reviewer asks for one transparency sentence (JOB-WOH-37:18 revise; shechaqim op revise): the canon's English edition reads 'the sky', so the canon is itself divided.

paragraphs.text: הֲלֹֽא־חָכְמָ֥ה תִקְרָ֑א וּ֝תְבוּנָ֗ה תִּתֵּ֥ן קוֹלָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: Does not wisdom call, and understanding raise her voice?

notes.official: *ḥokmâ* 'wisdom' and *tĕbûnâ* 'understanding' are personified with feminine verbs and pronouns ('her voice'). The line prints lower-case 'wisdom', as the ASV does, and lets the pronoun carry the personification; a capital would turn the figure into a name, which the Hebrew, having no capitals, does not mark (`chokhmah-personified-wisdom-proverbs`). Proverbs is new in the corpus; the Writings conventions apply (`poetic-lineation-and-speech-convention-writings`).

paragraphs.text: בְּרֹאשׁ־מְרוֹמִ֥ים עֲלֵי־דָ֑רֶךְ בֵּ֖ית נְתִיב֣וֹת נִצָּֽבָה׃

i18n.en: On the top of the heights beside the way, where the paths meet, she takes her stand;

notes.official: *bĕrōʾš-mĕrômîm* 'On the top of the heights'; *bêt nĕtîbôt* 'where the paths meet' (lit. 'the house of paths').

paragraphs.text: לְיַד־שְׁעָרִ֥ים לְפִי־קָ֑רֶת מְב֖וֹא פְתָחִ֣ים תָּרֹֽנָּה׃

i18n.en: beside the gates, at the mouth of the town, at the entrance of the doors, she cries aloud:

notes.official: *lĕpî-qāret* 'at the mouth of the town' (*qeret*, a poetic word for 'city'); *tārōnnâ* 'she cries aloud'. Wisdom's speech (vv 4-36) follows without quotation marks, as a speech that fills the chapter (`poetic-lineation-and-speech-convention-writings`).

paragraphs.text: אֲלֵיכֶ֣ם אִישִׁ֣ים אֶקְרָ֑א וְ֝קוֹלִ֗י אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃

i18n.en: To you, O men, I call, and my voice is to the sons of human.

notes.official: *ʾălêkem ʾîšîm ʾeqrāʾ wĕqôlî ʾel-bĕnê ʾādām* 'To you, O men, I call, and my voice is to the sons of human'. *ʾîšîm* is a rare plural of *ʾîš* 'man' (Isa 53:3; Ps 141:4). The anarthrous *bĕnê ʾādām* is rendered as the central `ben-adam` entry renders the singular ('son of human'); the articular *bĕnê hāʾādām* (Ps 33:13; Eccl 3) is 'the sons of the human', as genesis-woh 11:5 under `ha-adam` (ASV 'the sons of men'; `adam-enosh-ish-human-terms-writings`). The same at v 31.

paragraphs.text: הָבִ֣ינוּ פְתָאיִ֣ם עָרְמָ֑ה וּ֝כְסִילִ֗ים הָבִ֥ינוּ לֵֽב׃

i18n.en: You simple ones, understand prudence; and you fools, gain an understanding heart.

notes.official: *pĕtāʾyim* 'simple ones'; *ʿormâ* 'prudence', the shrewdness of 1:4, here a virtue; *hābînû lēb* 'gain an understanding heart' (lit. 'understand heart').

paragraphs.text: שִׁ֭מְעוּ כִּֽי־נְגִידִ֣ים אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וּמִפְתַּ֥ח שְׂ֝פָתַ֗י מֵישָׁרִֽים׃

i18n.en: Hear, for I will speak noble things, and the opening of my lips will be right things.

notes.official: *nĕgîdîm* 'noble things' (lit. 'princely things'); *mêšārîm* 'right things'.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־אֱ֭מֶת יֶהְגֶּ֣ה חִכִּ֑י וְתוֹעֲבַ֖ת שְׂפָתַ֣י רֶֽשַׁע׃

i18n.en: For my mouth will utter truth, and wickedness is an abomination to my lips.

notes.official: *kî-ʾĕmet yehgeh ḥikkî* 'For my mouth will utter truth' (*ḥēk* 'palate'); *wĕtôʿăbat śĕpātay rešaʿ* 'and wickedness is an abomination to my lips' (central `toevah-abomination-cross-corpus-keyword`).

paragraphs.text: בְּצֶ֥דֶק כָּל־אִמְרֵי־פִ֑י אֵ֥ין בָּ֝הֶ֗ם נִפְתָּ֥ל וְעִקֵּֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: All the words of my mouth are in righteousness; there is nothing twisted or crooked in them.

paragraphs.text: כֻּלָּ֣ם נְ֭כֹחִים לַמֵּבִ֑ין וִֽ֝ישָׁרִ֗ים לְמֹ֣צְאֵי דָֽעַת׃

i18n.en: They are all straightforward to the one who understands, and right to those who find knowledge.

paragraphs.text: קְחֽוּ־מוּסָרִ֥י וְאַל־כָּ֑סֶף וְ֝דַ֗עַת מֵחָר֥וּץ נִבְחָֽר׃

i18n.en: Take my instruction, and not silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־טוֹבָ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה מִפְּנִינִ֑ים וְכָל־חֲ֝פָצִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִֽשְׁווּ־בָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: For wisdom is better than rubies, and all things that may be desired cannot compare with her.

notes.official: *kî-ṭôbâ ḥokmâ mippĕnînîm* 'For wisdom is better than rubies' (ASV; *pĕnînîm* may be corals or pearls). The verse speaks of wisdom in the third person inside her own speech (cf. 3:15) (`chokhmah-personified-wisdom-proverbs`).

paragraphs.text: אֲ‍ֽנִי־חָ֭כְמָה שָׁכַ֣נְתִּי עָרְמָ֑ה וְדַ֖עַת מְזִמּ֣וֹת אֶמְצָֽא׃

i18n.en: I, wisdom, dwell with prudence, and I find out knowledge of discretion.

notes.official: *ʾănî-ḥokmâ šākantî ʿormâ* 'I, wisdom, dwell with prudence' (`chokhmah-personified-wisdom-proverbs`); *daʿat mĕzimmôt* 'knowledge of discretion'.

paragraphs.text: יִֽרְאַ֣ת יְהוָה֮ שְֽׂנֹ֫את רָ֥ע גֵּ֘אָ֤ה וְגָא֨וֹן ׀ וְדֶ֣רֶךְ רָ֭ע וּפִ֨י תַהְפֻּכ֬וֹת שָׂנֵֽאתִי׃

i18n.en: The fear of YHWH is to hate evil; pride and arrogance, and the evil way, and the perverse mouth I hate.

notes.official: The first clause (*yirʾat YHWH śĕnōʾt rāʿ* 'The fear of YHWH is to hate evil') interrupts Wisdom's first-person speech and is often taken as a gloss; it is in all witnesses and is translated.

paragraphs.text: לִֽי־עֵ֭צָה וְתוּשִׁיָּ֑ה אֲנִ֥י בִ֝ינָ֗ה לִ֣י גְבוּרָֽה׃

i18n.en: Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom; I am understanding; might is mine.

notes.official: *tûšiyyâ* 'sound wisdom', practical competence; *ʾănî bînâ* 'I am understanding'.

paragraphs.text: בִּ֭י מְלָכִ֣ים יִמְלֹ֑כוּ וְ֝רוֹזְנִ֗ים יְחֹ֣קְקוּ צֶֽדֶק׃

i18n.en: By me kings reign, and rulers decree what is just.

notes.official: *rôzĕnîm yĕḥōqĕqû ṣedeq* 'rulers decree what is just'.

paragraphs.text: בִּ֭י שָׂרִ֣ים יָשֹׂ֑רוּ וּ֝נְדִיבִ֗ים כָּל־שֹׁ֥פְטֵי צֶֽדֶק׃

i18n.en: By me princes rule, and nobles — all who judge righteously.

notes.official: *bî śārîm yāśōrû ûnĕdîbîm kol-šōpṭê ṣedeq* 'By me princes rule, and nobles — all who judge righteously'. The Leningrad Codex reads *ṣedeq* 'righteousness'; many Hebrew manuscripts, the LXX and the ASV read *ʾāreṣ* ('all the judges of the earth'). The MT is translated and the variant recorded (`mt-baseline-versification-and-psalm-numbering-writings`).

paragraphs.text: אֲ֭נִי אהביה [אֹהֲבַ֣י] אֵהָ֑ב וּ֝מְשַׁחֲרַ֗י יִמְצָאֻֽנְנִי׃

i18n.en: I love those who love me, and those who seek me diligently will find me.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: Ketiv *ʾhbyh* 'those who love her' / Qere *ʾōhăbay* 'those who love me'. The Qere, which fits the first-person speech, is translated (ASV the same; `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-writings`). *mĕšaḥăray* 'those who seek me diligently' (*šḥr* 'seek earnestly').

paragraphs.text: עֹֽשֶׁר־וְכָב֥וֹד אִתִּ֑י ה֥וֹן עָ֝תֵ֗ק וּצְדָקָֽה׃

i18n.en: Riches and honor are with me, enduring wealth and righteousness.

notes.official: *hôn ʿātēq* 'enduring wealth'; *ṣĕdāqâ* 'righteousness' (in this context also 'prosperity').

paragraphs.text: ט֣וֹב פִּ֭רְיִי מֵחָר֣וּץ וּמִפָּ֑ז וּ֝תְבוּאָתִ֗י מִכֶּ֥סֶף נִבְחָֽר׃

i18n.en: My fruit is better than gold, even fine gold, and my yield than choice silver.

paragraphs.text: בְּאֹֽרַח־צְדָקָ֥ה אֲהַלֵּ֑ך בְּ֝ת֗וֹךְ נְתִיב֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט׃

i18n.en: I walk in the way of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of justice,

paragraphs.text: לְהַנְחִ֖יל אֹהֲבַ֥י ׀ יֵ֑שׁ וְאֹצְרֹ֖תֵיהֶ֣ם אֲמַלֵּֽא׃ (פ)

i18n.en: to cause those who love me to inherit substance, and I will fill their treasuries.

notes.official: *lĕhanḥîl ʾōhăbay yēš* 'to cause those who love me to inherit substance': *yēš* 'there is' is used here as a noun, 'substance, wealth' (ASV). The petucha (פ) after the verse closes the first part of the speech.

paragraphs.text: יְֽהוָ֗ה קָ֭נָנִי רֵאשִׁ֣ית דַּרְכּ֑וֹ קֶ֖דֶם מִפְעָלָ֣יו מֵאָֽז׃

i18n.en: YHWH created me at the beginning of his way, before his works of old.

notes.official:
*YHWH qānānî rēʾšît darkô qedem mipʿālāyw mēʾāz* 'YHWH created me at the beginning of his way, before his works of old'. *qānānî* is the verse's crux. The verb *qnh* usually means 'acquire, possess' (ASV 'possessed'; Aquila, Symmachus and Theodotion *ektēsato*; Vulgate *possedit*), but in divine contexts it also means 'create, produce, beget' (Gen 14:19, 22; Deut 32:6), with cognates in Ugaritic *qny* and Phoenician *ʾl qn ʾrṣ* (KAI 26). The LXX *ektisen*, the Targum and the Peshitta have 'created', and so do NRSV and NJPS. The birth verbs of vv 24-25 (*ḥôlāltî* 'I was brought forth') favour a sense of origin; Vawter (*JBL* 99, 1980) argues for 'acquire'. The line applies the central `koneh-shamayim-va-aretz`, which already lists this verse. The central `reshit-darkhei-el` quoted the verse with the ASV 'possessed', and this wave proposes correcting that quotation (wave-W1 central diff). The fourth-century Arian controversy turned on the LXX *ektisen* of this verse.

*rēʾšît darkô* is taken adverbially, 'at the beginning of his way' (ASV, NRSV, NJPS). It can also be appositional, 'as the first of his way', the construction of Job 40:19 (*rēʾšît darkê-ʾēl* 'the first of the ways of El', central `reshit-darkhei-el`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes vv 22-23, 27 and 29-31 ('Iahvé m'a créée, principe de sa voie ...'; English 'Yahweh possessed me in the beginning of his way') and reads Wisdom as the intelligence and science by which the creators made the dry land and the living beings on it, and which now leads humanity toward repeating their creators' acts. The line's 'created' follows the central lexical entry. It agrees with the canon's French and differs from the canon's English 'possessed'.

paragraphs.text: מֵ֭עוֹלָם נִסַּ֥כְתִּי מֵרֹ֗אשׁ מִקַּדְמֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: From everlasting I was set up, from the beginning, from the earliest times of the earth.

notes.official: *mēʿôlām nissaktî mērōʾš miqqadmê-ʾāreṣ* 'From everlasting I was set up, from the beginning, from the earliest times of the earth'. *nissaktî* is taken from *nsk* II 'install' (cf. Ps 2:6; ASV 'set up'). A derivation from *skk* 'weave' ('I was woven', cf. Ps 139:13) is also proposed and is not adopted. *miqqadmê-ʾāreṣ* 'from the earliest times of the earth' (ASV 'before the earth was'; `eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`). See the reception note at v 22.

paragraphs.text: בְּאֵין־תְּהֹמ֥וֹת חוֹלָ֑לְתִּי בְּאֵ֥ין מַ֝עְיָנ֗וֹת נִכְבַּדֵּי־מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: When there were no depths I was brought forth, when there were no springs heavy with water.

notes.official: *bĕʾên-tĕhōmôt ḥôlāltî* 'When there were no depths I was brought forth': *ḥôlāltî* (Polal of *ḥyl* 'writhe in labour') is birth language, as in v 25 and Ps 90:2. *tĕhōmôt* 'depths' (central `tehom`); *maʿyānôt nikbaddê-māyim* 'springs heavy with water'.

paragraphs.text: בְּטֶ֣רֶם הָרִ֣ים הָטְבָּ֑עוּ לִפְנֵ֖י גְבָע֣וֹת חוֹלָֽלְתִּי׃

i18n.en: Before the mountains were sunk, before the hills, I was brought forth,

notes.official: *bĕṭerem hārîm hoṭbāʿû* 'Before the mountains were sunk': the Hophal of *ṭbʿ* 'sink' is rendered as in job-woh 38:6 ('its bases sunk'), the mountains sunk into their foundations (ASV 'settled').

paragraphs.text: עַד־לֹ֣א עָ֭שָׂה אֶ֣רֶץ וְחוּצ֑וֹת וְ֝רֹ֗אשׁ עָפְר֥וֹת תֵּבֵֽל׃

i18n.en: while as yet he had not made the earth and the open fields, nor the first of the dust of the world.

notes.official: *ʿad-lōʾ ʿāśâ ʾereṣ wĕḥûṣôt* 'while as yet he had not made the earth and the open fields' (*ḥûṣôt* 'outside places'); *rōʾš ʿaprôt tēbēl* 'the first of the dust of the world'. *ʾereṣ* || *tēbēl* is cosmic, so 'earth' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`).

paragraphs.text: בַּהֲכִינ֣וֹ שָׁ֭מַיִם שָׁ֣ם אָ֑נִי בְּח֥וּקוֹ ח֝֗וּג עַל־פְּנֵ֥י תְהֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: When he established the skies, I was there; when he inscribed a circle on the face of the deep,

notes.official: *bahăkînô šāmayim šām ʾānî* 'When he established the skies, I was there': the sky of creation, 'skies' under the central `shamayim` rule (ASV 'the heavens'; the canon's French 'les cieux'). *bĕḥûqô ḥûg ʿal-pĕnê tĕhôm* 'when he inscribed a circle on the face of the deep': *ḥûg* is the circle of the horizon or of the vault (Isa 40:22; Job 26:10), traced on *tĕhôm* (central `tehom`; *ʿal-pĕnê tĕhôm* as Gen 1:2). See the reception note at v 22.

paragraphs.text: בְּאַמְּצ֣וֹ שְׁחָקִ֣ים מִמָּ֑עַל בַּ֝עֲז֗וֹז עִינ֥וֹת תְּהוֹם׃

i18n.en: when he made firm the clouds above, when the springs of the deep grew strong,

notes.official: *bĕʾammĕṣô šĕḥāqîm mimmāʿal* 'when he made firm the clouds above'. *šĕḥāqîm* is 'clouds' under the new central `shechaqim-clouds-cross-corpus` (KJV 'clouds'; ASV and NRSV 'skies'; NJPS 'heavens'), as at job-woh 38:37 and Job 37:18, 21. With 'clouds' the two words of vv 27-28, *šāmayim* and *šĕḥāqîm*, have two English words, as in the pair of job-woh 38:37 ('the clouds ... the skies'). *baʿăzôz ʿînôt tĕhôm* 'when the springs of the deep grew strong' (`tehom`).

paragraphs.text: בְּשׂ֘וּמ֤וֹ לַיָּ֨ם ׀ חֻקּ֗וֹ וּ֭מַיִם לֹ֣א יַֽעַבְרוּ־פִ֑יו בְּ֝חוּק֗וֹ מ֣וֹסְדֵי אָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: when he set for the sea its boundary, that the waters should not pass beyond his command, when he marked out the foundations of the earth,

notes.official: *bĕśûmô layyām ḥuqqô* 'when he set for the sea its boundary': *ḥōq* 'limit' is rendered as in job-woh 38:10 ('my boundary'). The verse shares the sea-restraint motif of central `gevul-yam` (Job 38:8-11), whose rationale cites it. *ûmayim lōʾ yaʿabrû-pîw* 'that the waters should not pass beyond his command' (lit. 'his mouth'; ASV 'commandment'). *bĕḥûqô môsĕdê ʾāreṣ* 'when he marked out the foundations of the earth' (`eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`). See the reception note at v 22.

paragraphs.text: וָֽאֶהְיֶ֥ה אֶצְל֗וֹ אָ֫מ֥וֹן וָֽאֶהְיֶ֣ה שַׁ֭עֲשֻׁעִים י֤וֹם ׀ י֑וֹם מְשַׂחֶ֖קֶת לְפָנָ֣יו בְּכָל־עֵֽת׃

i18n.en: then I was beside him, a master workman, and I was delight day by day, rejoicing before him at all times,

notes.official:
*wāʾehyeh ʾeṣlô ʾāmôn* 'then I was beside him, a master workman'. *ʾāmôn* has three main explanations: 'master workman, craftsman' (ASV; NRSV 'master worker'; cf. Akkadian *ummânu* 'craftsman, sage', *hāʾāmôn* Jer 52:15, *ʾommān* 'artist' Song 7:2, and Wis 7:21 *technitis*); 'nursling, little child', reading *ʾāmûn* (Aquila; Fox, AB 18A); or the adverb 'constantly, faithfully' (*ʾĕmûn*). The line keeps the ASV (`amon-master-workman-proverbs-8-30`, inferred). *šaʿăšuʿîm yôm yôm* 'delight day by day' (the ASV supplies 'his'); *mĕśaḥeqet lĕpānāyw* 'rejoicing before him' (*śḥq* 'play, make merry').

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The canon's French quotation (see v 22) has 'j'étais à son côté, comme architecte', the craftsman reading of *ʾāmôn*; its English edition has 'then I was by him, as one brought up with him', the nursling reading. The canon itself is divided, and the line follows the ASV, not either wording.

paragraphs.text: מְ֭שַׂחֶקֶת בְּתֵבֵ֣ל אַרְצ֑וֹ וְ֝שַׁעֲשֻׁעַ֗י אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: rejoicing in the inhabited world of his earth, and my delights were with the sons of human.

notes.official: *mĕśaḥeqet bĕtēbēl ʾarṣô* 'rejoicing in the inhabited world of his earth' (ASV 'in his habitable earth'; `eretz-earth-and-land-scope-writings`). *wĕšaʿăšuʿay ʾet-bĕnê ʾādām* 'and my delights were with the sons of human': anarthrous, under `ben-adam` (see v 4). The canon's French ('mes délices sont avec les fils d'homme') has the same anarthrous form; see the reception note at v 22.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה בָ֭נִים שִׁמְעוּ־לִ֑י וְ֝אַשְׁרֵ֗י דְּרָכַ֥י יִשְׁמֹֽרוּ׃

i18n.en: And now, sons, listen to me: blessed are those who keep my ways.

notes.official: *wĕʿattâ bānîm šimʿû-lî* 'And now, sons, listen to me'. *ʾašrê* 'blessed' (ASV; NJPS 'happy'), as at Ps 33:12; the same at v 34.

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְע֖וּ מוּסָ֥ר וַחֲכָ֗מוּ וְאַל־תִּפְרָֽעוּ׃

i18n.en: Hear instruction and be wise, and do not neglect it.

notes.official: *wĕʾal-tiprāʿû* 'and do not neglect it' (*prʿ* 'let go, let loose').

paragraphs.text: אַ֥שְֽׁרֵי אָדָם֮ שֹׁמֵ֪עַֽ֫ לִ֥י לִשְׁקֹ֣ד עַל־דַּ֭לְתֹתַי י֤וֹם ׀ י֑וֹם לִ֝שְׁמֹ֗ר מְזוּזֹ֥ת פְּתָחָֽי׃

i18n.en: Blessed is the human who listens to me, watching at my doors day by day, waiting at the posts of my doorways.

notes.official: *ʾašrê ʾādām šōmēaʿ lî* 'Blessed is the human who listens to me': *ʾādām* is 'the human', on the job-woh and genesis-woh pattern (central `ha-adam`; ASV 'the man'; `adam-enosh-ish-human-terms-writings`). *mĕzûzōt pĕtāḥāy* 'the posts of my doorways'.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י מֹ֭צְאִי מצאי [מָצָ֣א] חַיִּ֑ים וַיָּ֥פֶק רָ֝צ֗וֹן מֵיְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: For whoever finds me has found life, and obtains favor from YHWH.

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere: the line reads *mōṣĕʾî mṣʾy [māṣāʾ] ḥayyîm*. Ketiv *mṣʾy* (*mōṣĕʾê*, 'those who find me are finders of life') / Qere *māṣāʾ* 'whoever finds me has found life'. The Qere is translated (ASV 'findeth'; `ketiv-qere-qere-translated-writings`). *wayyāpeq rāṣôn* 'and obtains favor'.

paragraphs.text: וְֽ֭חֹטְאִי חֹמֵ֣ס נַפְשׁ֑וֹ כָּל־מְ֝שַׂנְאַ֗י אָ֣הֲבוּ מָֽוֶת׃ (פ)

i18n.en: But he who misses me wrongs his own life; all who hate me love death.

notes.official: *wĕḥōṭĕʾî ḥōmēs napšô* 'But he who misses me wrongs his own life'. *ḥṭʾ* is 'miss (the mark)', the antithesis of *mōṣĕʾî* 'whoever finds me' in v 35 (ASV 'he that sinneth against me'). *napšô* is 'his own life' because the two verses set life against death, the case in which the corpus renders *nepeš* 'life' (`nefesh-scope-writings`; ASV 'his own soul'; NRSV 'injure themselves'). *kol-mĕśanʾay ʾāhăbû māwet* 'all who hate me love death'.
